newsitem.title: USA: GM's Chevrolet unit sees 1997 sales gains.
newsitem.headline: GM's Chevrolet unit sees 1997 sales gains.

text.p: General Motors Corp's Chevrolet division expects its total 1997 sales to climb to more than 2.6 million from 2.5 million last year, General Manager John Middlebrook said on Monday.
Middlebrook said Chevrolet, GM's largest division, also expected to increase its share of the U.S. car market from 12.2 percent and its share in trucks from 28 percent.
"We expect to be better in both of those car and truck numbers for 1997," said Middlebrook, who spoke at the North American International Auto Show.
Middlebrook's comments followed the introduction of the 1998 Chevrolet Corvette at the show.
Separately, Richard Wagoner, president of GM's North American auto operations, said GM's production volume and dealer stock would not improve much until the second half of 1997.
The automaker is in the process of launching 15 new cars and trucks in the United States.
GM expects its share of the U.S. market to increase from the 31 percent it commanded at the end of 1996, Wagoner said. But he cautioned that the model changeovers would hamper any improvement.
"We'll make a start next year to what I'd say is a more normal level of penetration, which is probably in the 33 percent range," he said. "I'm not sure we can get that far this year."
